rules: Preserve plot, lore, reveals, outcomes, and established character identities.
Do not silently replace established terminology without recording the change.
Skull-Veil is the established nickname for the Elven faction; the hostile creatures from the sky require their own separate creature name.
High Elven language used by Kael-Vossen's court must remain original, varied, and translator-friendly.
Lyra learned High Elven from archives and treaties and is therefore capable but somewhat rusty when speaking it spontaneously.
High Elven dialogue should appear naturally and substantially when the scene involves Elven speakers; it should not replace every line of readable dialogue.
The commander and Kael-Vossen citizens should retain believable hatred and fear toward House Valerius and toward outsiders associated with Abel where the manuscript establishes that reaction.
The hostile sky creatures must remain frightening and distinct from the Skull-Veil Elves.
D&D terminology and fantasy races/creatures can inform the world, but Aethelgard's specific lore and descriptions remain original.
Avoid overusing a single generic term such as ledger when a contextually accurate established alternative exists.
